items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I became acquainted with some Philippine musicians... one who played trombone called himself Felix the Cat.

ctx.x: One day while walking downtown, I was surprised to see an ex-bandleader of mine. It was Teddy who had an orchestra in the Savoy Ballroom when I came to France in 1935. Teddy told me that he had done service in Europe and was supposed to have been discharged and sent back to New York from Germany but he had a run in with an officer and told him that he had been manager of a club in New York which seemed to have been a better position in civil life than the officer had and this officer arranged to have Teddy sent…

I became acquainted with some Philippine musicians but how this happened, I do not recall. However, it happened and one who played trombone called himself Felix the Cat. He had played in Japan before the war and told me that he had been associated with an American trombone player known as Slick. I had known Slick also because he had been in Cincinnati for a while and he also played trumpet. He was the first trumpet player I had ever known that played trombone or visa versa, But I never knew his real name.

Felix played with an orchestra, all Philippines, that had 16 musicians. And if you closed your eyes or only heard them playing if you were coming into a dance hall, you would bet your bottom dollar that it was the Glenn Miller band playing an engagement while passing through Manila. The only weakness was in the solos. But the sound was there.
